title: Cross-region traffic washout led to degraded tail latencies and circuit-breaker desync
creator: Nina Rodriguez
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 between 08:13-08:46 UTC we observed a multi-region SLO miss for host-side 99th percentile latency for generation endpoints. The observable symptom was an extended tail in request latency in region eu-west-1 that propagated to us-west-2 via our regional affinity routing and triggered a cascade of circuit-breaker openings and aggressive load-shedding. Total affected requests: ~1.1M tokens; impacted customers: 9 paying customers with latency-sensitive SLAs. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation, and concrete follow-ups.
timeline: 08:12 UTC - traffic spike (bot-indexing) detected in eu-west-1; 90th pct tokens per request increased by ~3x
08:13 UTC - per-region router started sticky-region reroutes due to client affinity, increasing eu-west-1 queue depth
08:18 UTC - KV cache warmup deficit observed on a subset of shards (cold hot-shard rotation after prior maintenance)
08:21 UTC - eu-west-1 autoscaler began scale-up but provisioned with cold instances (slow kernel warm paths)
08:25 UTC - local circuit-breaker hysteresis is misconfigured: open threshold was short, close threshold long, leading to asymmetric CB openings
08:27 UTC - control plane heartbeat laged 2s due to DB replica lag; some routers evaluated region-health stale and routed additional traffic to secondary region us-west-2
08:30 UTC - us-west-2 experienced a sudden influx; its circuit-breakers began opening, but their backoff schedules were unsynchronized with eu-west-1, causing oscillation
08:36 UTC - global fallback policy triggered cross-region failover; KV caches were not primed, increasing token generation latency and amplifying shedding
08:46 UTC - majority of circuits recovered after manual throttling rule and explicit warm-cache priming; SLOs rejoined baseline by 09:10 UTC
root_cause: A confluence of: (1) an unexpected traffic washout (long-tail bot-generated requests) in eu-west-1; (2) asymmetric circuit-breaker hysteresis parameters that opened eu-west-1 circuits aggressively but closed them slowly, preventing quick recovery; (3) unsynchronized region-health evaluation across routers due to control-plane heartbeat lag; (4) cold KV caches on newly provisioned nodes caused per-request work to spike; and (5) our failover policy moved traffic between regions without cache priming or coordinated CB backoff, amplifying latency and load shedding.
contributing_factors: Recent maintenance rotated hot shards and left caches cold on a subset of instances
CB hysteresis defaults were tuned for single-region faults, not joint-region oscillations
Control-plane replica lag (DB) under spike caused delayed region-health signals
Autoscaler bootstrapped instances with conservative kernel selection resulting in slower early-response paths
No pre-failover cache-warm path in the global routing policy
mitigation_taken_during_incident: 08:32 UTC - Applied temporary per-client rate limits for high-volume API keys to reduce bot noise
08:37 UTC - Manually adjusted CB close thresholds to shorten hysteresis on eu-west-1
08:40 UTC - Pushed a hot-cache prefill job for affected shards and prioritized KV serving threads
08:44 UTC - Enabled manual cross-region throttling gate to slow failover transfers into us-west-2
impact_summary: SLO: generation 99th-pct latency exceeded 2x target for 33 minutes. Behavioral impact included increased token cost and customer-visible latency for real-time features. Internal pager alerts triggered and on-call rotation responded. No data loss or security compromise.
postmortem_analysis: The immediate cause was operational (traffic spike) but our systems amplified the effect through misaligned guardrails: the circuit-breaker parameters and failover orchestration are tuned independently per region which allowed oscillatory behavior. Our autoscaler and runtime warm-paths are not guaranteed during fast scale-up, so failover should not rely on cold path performance. The control plane's health signals need stricter SLAs and backpressure on routing decisions during DB replica lag.
action_items: ENG-98123-A1: Introduce a coordinated CB policy: central config that ensures symmetric open/close windows across regions and a randomized backoff jitter. Owner: Marco Liu. Due: 2026-03-24
ENG-98123-A2: Add a pre-failover cache priming step in the global routing policy; implement cheap async priming when failover starts. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-03-31
ENG-98123-A3: Harden control-plane health signals: instrument DB replica lag metrics into region-health evaluation and set conservative thresholds. Owner: Rajiv Menon. Due: 2026-03-21
ENG-98123-A4: Update autoscaler bootstrapping to prefer warm kernel paths or prioritize quick KV thread spin-up; add integration test for warmup latency. Owner: Sofie Berg. Due: 2026-04-07
ENG-98123-A5: Implement caller-level bot-detection and temporary client soft-quota enforcement to blunt sudden indexing traffic. Owner: Priya Chauhan. Due: 2026-03-28
ENG-98123-A6: Run a chaos experiment simulating joint-region spikes with CB hysteresis and failover to validate changes. Owner: Reliability Eng Team. Due: 2026-04-14

outcome: Short-term mitigations restored SLOs within 40 minutes. The engineering team agrees on a multi-pronged follow-up: centralize circuit-breaker config, add pre-failover cache priming, harden control plane health signals, and improve autoscaler warm-path behavior. Owners assigned and timelines set. This postmortem will be reviewed in the reliability guild on 2026-03-18.
